skills_considered.reason: The review yields a mechanistic question and no therapeutic candidate; forging a portfolio would overstate synthesis as intervention evidence.
No drug, compound or exposure emerged from this review, so there is no candidate for the safety gate.
No BATCH_COMMIT was authorised or needed; the four canonical scientific current files remain unchanged.

group_assessment.weighting: PubMed author counts measured 2026-08-06 for Aldaz CM[Author] (138) and Aldaz CM[Author] AND WWOX (38). Aldaz is a founding/primary WWOX gene laboratory, and Hussain is an experimental WWOX co-author; the group is not a primary clinical WWOX-DEE cohort group. Here the evidence type is mixed but synthesis-dominant: narrative review plus re-analysis/visualisation of public expression resources, with primary wet-lab results imported from cited papers. Gene expertise raises confidence in field coverage and biological context, but it cannot raise a cross-paper mechanistic bridge to causal evidence. Observations from public datasets and interpretations of mediation are therefore weighted separately.

field_density.note: The WWOX-by-myelin and WWOX-by-oligodendrocyte intersections remain small. That makes the review's bridge useful as a search map, not strong by repetition; the direct primary experiments must bear any causal conclusion.

multihop.note: The 86 XML references were enumerated after sequential reading. Twenty-six title-direct WWOX/disease/mechanism references carry PMIDs. Twenty-five resolve in the paper registry, tracking log, batch queue or research queue. PMID 17470496, the pre-gene linkage paper for the 16q21-q23 SCAR locus, is absent from those five structured files; it is bibliographic lineage rather than a load-bearing mechanism and is recorded in the durable dossier. The primary GABA and interactome debts were already FT-008/FT-038; the lipid and rat-myelin primaries are newly FT-039/FT-040.

corpus_crossquery.query: Which of the review's 26 WWOX-/disease-/mechanism-direct PMID references occur in paper_registry_current.md, and which mechanistic conclusions already have stronger primary anchors in claims and discovery entries?
corpus_crossquery.note: Mechanical post-reading audit: 23 of 26 direct PMIDs occur in paper_registry_current.md; 11719429 and 30094525 occur in other structured queues and 17470496 occurs in none of the five structured files checked. Existing CLAIM 003/004/005/026 and DL-MECH-010/012/018/031 already contain stronger primary evidence than this review for myelin, GABA/glia, inflammation and trafficking.

retraction_check.result: No retraction, expression of concern or correction was returned for any of the 16 batch records, including PMID 33255508, by the intake retraction gate on 2026-08-06. The Europe PMC full-text record is PMCID PMC7727818 and the article is open access.

entries.proposition: The OPC observation is lineage expression, not evidence that WWOX acts cell-autonomously in oligodendrocytes.
entries.snippet: Within the oligodendrocyte population, the highest Wwox expression levels are observed in progenitor oligodendrocytes, with significantly lower levels in mature myelinated oligodendrocytes
entries.anchor: Section 2, WWOX Expression in CNS, BrainRNAseq paragraph

entries.proposition: The review's LPS result is a descriptive expression response in public mouse microglia data.
entries.snippet: substantial upregulation of Wwox expression can be observed in microglial cells upon treatment of mice with lipopolysaccharide (LPS) used as an inflammatogenic agent
entries.anchor: Section 2, WWOX Expression in CNS, Figure 3d discussion

entries.proposition: As of the review's cutoff, Q230P recurred in eight reported WOREE cases from six families.
entries.snippet: the p.Gln230Pro mutation was found both as a biallelic mutation and also in heterozygous compound cases combined with other mutations and has been reported in a total of 8 WOREE cases affecting a total of 6 different families
entries.anchor: Section 3.2, WWOX-Related Early Infantile Epileptic Encephalopathy

entries.proposition: The authors explicitly acknowledge that the molecular effects of most missense variants were unknown.
entries.snippet: Currently, the mechanistic effects of most of the observed missense mutations on WWOX function are not known

entries.proposition: The GABA synthesis finding is a reviewed primary result from Wwox-null hippocampus, not a new experiment in this review.
entries.snippet: We also observed reduced expression of glutamic acid decarboxylase proteins GAD65/67 in Wwox null hippocampi; these are the principal enzymes responsible for GABA synthesis
entries.anchor: Section 3.3, Evidence from Rodent Models of Wwox Ablation

entries.proposition: The lipid and trafficking routes are presented as two potential themes linking WWOX to myelin, not as tested mediators.
entries.snippet: Two mechanistic themes potentially link WWOX with myelogenesis. First, as mentioned in the AD section, there is strong evidence for WWOX to play a role in cellular lipid homeostasis
entries.anchor: Section 3.6, WWOX, Multiple Sclerosis, and Myelination

entries.proposition: The review labels the WWOX-myelin connection as a suggestion arising from the assembled observations.
entries.snippet: The sum of the described observations suggests that a mechanistic association between WWOX and myelination likely exists

entries.proposition: The source itself identifies constitutive knockout lifespan as a limitation requiring conditional and longer-lived models.
entries.snippet: given the very limited lifespan of Wwox-KO mice, new conditional targeted models and models with longer lifespan are needed to provide more valuable mechanistic insights
